  1. Multi-node LLM

Multi-node LLM

For models that do not fit on the GPUs of a single node. Adding a worker key enables LeaderWorkerSet-based serving.

Prerequisites 

kubectl get crd leaderworkersets.leaderworkerset.x-k8s.io
kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.'nvidia\.com/gpu'

Multi-node serving requires fast node-to-node networking. Without RDMA or high-bandwidth interconnect, throughput suffers badly.

Complete values file

Two nodes with four GPUs each, tensor parallel four.

namespace: models

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: false
  name: hf-secret

llmDefaults:
  image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-70b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
      name: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --served-model-name
      - llama-3.1-70b-instruct
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "4"
      - --max-model-len
      - "8192"
      - --dtype
      - bfloat16
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "16"
        memory: 128Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "4"
    parallelism:
      tensor: 4
      data: 8
      dataLocal: 4
    worker: {}

Parallelism keys

Key Meaning
tensor GPUs splitting each layer; usually the per-node GPU count
pipeline Stages splitting layers across groups
data Total GPUs across the deployment
dataLocal GPUs per node

Node count is data / dataLocal. Above, 8 / 4 gives two nodes.

parallelism.tensor and --tensor-parallel-size must agree with the GPU limit per pod. Mismatches cause startup failures or silent under-use.

Sizing examples

Model dtype Total GPU memory Layout
70B bfloat16 ~140 GB plus cache 2 nodes x 4 x 40 GB
70B bfloat16 ~140 GB plus cache 1 node x 8 x 80 GB
405B bfloat16 ~810 GB plus cache 4 nodes x 8 x 80 GB
405B FP8 ~405 GB plus cache 2 nodes x 8 x 80 GB

Single node with eight GPUs, no worker needed:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-70b-single-node
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "8"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "32"
        memory: 256Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "8"

Very large models

Four nodes with eight GPUs each, combining tensor and pipeline parallelism:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-405b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "8"
      - --pipeline-parallel-size
      - "4"
      - --max-model-len
      - "4096"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "64"
        memory: 512Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
    parallelism:
      tensor: 8
      pipeline: 4
      data: 32
      dataLocal: 8
    worker: {}

Different worker shape

Workers reuse the leader definition unless overridden:

    worker:
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models
        - --tensor-parallel-size
        - "4"
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "16"
          memory: 128Gi
          nvidia.com/gpu: "4"

Placing leader and worker on different hardware

Both pods accept scheduling fields. A worker inherits the leader’s placement unless it sets its own:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-70b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
    nodeSelector:
      accelerator: nvidia-h100
    tolerations:
      - key: nvidia.com/gpu
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
    parallelism:
      tensor: 4
      data: 8
      dataLocal: 4
    worker:
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: nvidia-a100
      priorityClassName: worker-priority

Here the leader lands on an H100 node, workers on A100 nodes, and the worker inherits the toleration because it does not define one. See GPU and scheduling.

Shared memory

Multi-node vLLM is sensitive to /dev/shm size. If you see Bus error or NCCL failures, raise it through an LLMInferenceServiceConfig referenced with baseRefs, or use a runtime that already sets a larger value.

Cold starts

A 70B model is roughly 140 GB of weights. Downloading that on every pod start is slow and expensive. Strongly consider:

  • Local model cache for node-local copies
  • A pvc:// source shared across pods
  • An in-region object storage mirror

Verify 

kubectl get llminferenceservice llama-70b -n models
kubectl get leaderworkerset -n models
kubectl get pods -n models -o wide

Leader and worker pods should be spread across nodes. Check GPU use on each:

kubectl exec -n models <leader-pod> -- nvidia-smi
kubectl exec -n models <worker-pod> -- nvidia-smi

Then test:

kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-70b 8080:80

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain tensor parallelism."}],
    "max_tokens": 256
  }'

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
Workers never become ready LeaderWorkerSet controller missing Install the controller
NCCL timeout Network too slow or blocked Check interconnect and network policy
Only leader uses GPUs Parallelism mismatch Align parallelism with vLLM arguments
Pods pending Not enough whole nodes free Free capacity or reduce data
Out of memory at load Context too large Lower --max-model-len
